what_this_is: DATA for do-work/pieces.mjs and do-work/piece-sweep.mjs, and for the two piece rows (tool:split-a-document-into-pieces and tool:check-every-piece-is-covered, both run by do-work/check-against-their-rules-and-verdicts.mjs with the row's name as its argument). A piece is a row of the person's one Checks list (list:checks, records `record_prefix`<id> of type `check_type`) whose `kind_field` is `piece_kind`. The coverage row reads the list only in pages: the ids of every row (fields []), then the piece rows by the door's where on that field, narrowed to the fields it reads, folded into a running tally. `answer`: the answer's room (`most_bytes`, the most bytes of JSON a run's answer takes, since a door carries it twice in one 65,536-byte message), the room kept for the cursor (`cursor_bytes`), how many uncovered pieces each file names over every file (`named_per_file`) and in one file's page (`named_in_one_file`), and how many missing checks are named (`missing_at_most`; their counts are whole). `split`: how the split row keeps a document's pieces (do-work/pieces.mjs keepPieces): a Namespace file is read by name in `read_bytes` pages, at most `most_file_bytes` in all; the piece rows already kept are read `reads_at_once` at a time; each write carries at most `write_rows` records and `write_bytes` bytes as the door carries them (the record and its expected value, quoted once more), under the door's 64 KiB message; `named_at_most` piece ids are named in the answer. `no_file`: the file a piece with no source counts under. `words`: every line and refusal, {name} filled from the answer.

words.file: {file}: {pieces} pieces, {with_check} with a check, {with_reason} with a recorded reason, {uncovered} uncovered
words.uncovered: Uncovered in {file}: {id} ({section}) has no check and no reason. Write a check row and name it in checked_by, or record no_check: { reason, covered_by }.
words.missing_check: {piece} names the check {check} in checked_by, which is not a row of list:checks.
words.missing_covered_by: {piece} names {check} in no_check.covered_by, which is not a row of list:checks.
words.no_pieces: The person has no piece rows (record:check rows with kind piece); split their documents into pieces first with tool:split-a-document-into-pieces.
words.text: Send text (the words of the document, as a string) or name (the name of one of the person's files, as /folder/file.md), not both.
words.file_name: file, when sent, is the document's name, as a string.
words.totals: {files} files, {pieces} pieces: {with_check} with a check, {with_reason} with a recorded reason, {uncovered} uncovered
words.no_such_file: No piece row names the file {file}. Send a file the answer over every file lists, or leave file out.
words.too_little_room: most_bytes {most_bytes} leaves no room for one file's line; send a larger most_bytes (at least 2000).
words.file_too_large: {name} is {bytes} bytes; the split reads at most {most} bytes of one file.
words.file_changed: {name} changed while it was read; send the request again.
words.file_unreadable: {name} could not be read as one of the person's files: {why}
words.too_large_piece: {id} ({section}) is {bytes} bytes as the door carries it, more than one write holds; it was not kept. Split that block in the document, or keep it by hand.
words.kept: {file}: {pieces} pieces, {new} kept as new rows, {sources_added} found again as a source of a row already kept, {unchanged} already kept as they are
